channel.title: Eager to Be Healthy - a Health and Happiness Podcast
channel.description:
The Eager to Be Healthy Podcast — hosted by Michael Scott Eger, health coach and wellness advocate — brings you inspiring health and happiness conversations that empower you to live a more vibrant, balanced life.

Join us for aspirational, real-talk episodes featuring everyday people who've overcome struggles with health, chronic illness, happiness, mental wellness, and personal growth. We dive deep into nutrition, healthy eating, food sensitivities, gluten-free living, being active, fitness motivation, social dynamics, relationships, love, sadness, emotional resilience, and the joy of building a perfect life — one that's truly happy and healthy.


The most powerful stories come from laypeople just like you — ordinary folks figuring out how to eat better, move more, feel better, and thrive without perfectionism. No experts-only vibes here — just authentic, relatable journeys that show transformation is possible.

I'm Michael Scott Eger, your host and guide. I help people eat better and have way more fun doing it. Growing up pre-internet, pre-cell phones, and pre-gluten-free era, I battled severe illness from childhood — multiple surgeries by age 15, endless doctors, and no real answers. In 1987, I discovered food was the root cause. Changing what I ate changed everything: better energy, clearer hearing, stronger school performance, and a new lease on life.


Over 30+ years of personal experimentation and helping others, I've built real knowledge on holistic wellness, natural healing through diet, and sustainable lifestyle changes. I healed myself first so I could pay it forward — because I know the deep pain of being sick and want no one else to suffer.


That's the heart of the Eager to Be Healthy Wellness Network — a community dedicated to wellness, nutrition tips, healthy living, happiness habits, and supporting each other on the path to feeling great.


Tune in for motivating, down-to-earth discussions on health transformation, mind-body connection, joyful eating, and living with more energy, purpose, and happiness. Subscribe now and start your journey to be Eager to Be Healthy! Eagertobehealthy.com

item.title: Eager to be Healthy - JR Rennie - When the Paycheck Stopped and the Calling Started
item.description:
JR Rennie spent nearly forty years running a custom software company. In 2015 the revenue dried up almost overnight. He kept the doors open so his employees and clients were covered, and he stopped paying himself. Ten years later that income is still gone. What he found instead was a calling: BrushFires Ministry, which he and his wife Buffy run to help believers discover the work they were built to do.


In this conversation we talk about what happens when the plan stops working. JR shares why he chose his team over his own paycheck, the day he said out loud, "I know you're behind this. What do you want?", and how months of prayer, scripture, and writing turned frustration into peace. He is honest about the hard parts too: marrying young, raising a son who has lived with epilepsy for forty years, and why faithful people still face tests.


JR unpacks the new wine and new wineskins metaphor, explains why he never prays for patience, and gives his short answer to how to be happy: love God and love other people. Michael shares the car crash that reminded him he was never alone.


Find JR at brushfires-digital.com. Free registration includes four books and a Romans 12 spiritual gifts assessment. The Design WorkShop helps you put your purpose into words.


This is a value-for-value podcast. Support the show at eagertobehealthy.com/support.

Always consult your healthcare provider before making changes based on health content.


Takeaways

- Happiness follows circumstances; joy grows from loving God and loving others

- A hard season can point you toward your real calling

- Faithful people still face tests, and God stays present through every one

- Shema: listen with the intent to act

- Serving others is the surest way out of your own misery

- Your purpose has no expiration date

- Daily bread covers your needs; gratitude covers the rest

item.title: Eager to be Healthy - Elizabeth Kipp - Pain Is a Signal, Not a Life Sentence
item.description:
Elizabeth Kipp is a chronic pain management specialist, addiction recovery coach, Ancestral Clearing® practitioner, and bestselling author of The Way Through Chronic Pain: Tools to Reclaim Your Healing Power. After more than forty years of severe chronic pain, anxiety, and panic attacks, and more than thirty years of prescribed opioid and benzodiazepine dependence following back injuries and surgeries, she got herself out first. Then she built the map so other people could follow.

In this conversation we talk about chronic pain as a nervous-system problem, not just a tissue problem. Pain is a signal the brain interprets. Stay in it long enough and the pathways rewire: more stress response, more hypersensitivity, more fight-or-flight. Long-term opioids and benzos can mask that signal without resolving it, and they often tax gut motility, breath, sleep, and the very neuroplastic recovery you need.

Elizabeth walks through de-identifying from pain: moving from "I am my diagnosis" to "this is sensory information moving through my body." She covers safety as a physiological requirement (you cannot digest well in fight-or-flight), trauma-informed breathwork and somatics for rapid down-regulation, Ancestral Clearing® for inherited survival stress that keeps the nervous system stuck, and practical recovery tools she used herself: sleep rhythm, anti-inflammatory nutrition, yoga, Tai Chi, and rebuilding trust in her own body.

Find Elizabeth at elizabeth-kipp.com. Book: The Way Through Chronic Pain. Free resource: 5 Ways to Relieve Stress, Anxiety, & Fear (https://bit.ly/5WaysToRelieveStress).

This is a value-for-value podcast. Support the show at eagertobehealthy.com/support.

Always consult your healthcare provider before making changes based on health content.

Takeaways

- Doing fine with chronic pain is not the same as being well

- Pain is a brain-interpreted signal; chronic pain rewires the nervous system

- Long-term opioids and benzos often mask symptoms without resolving root signaling

- De-identify from pain: sensory information, not identity

- Safety first: digestion, breath, and recovery fail in fight-or-flight

- Ancestral Clearing® and trauma-informed breathwork can release stuck survival patterns

- Small daily practices (sleep, food, breath, movement)

rebuild capacity

item.title: Eager to be Healthy - Dr. Radhika Achari - Doing Fine Is Not the Same as Being Well
item.description:
Dr. Radhika Achari is a board-certified behavior analyst with more than fifteen years of clinical work. She has spent her career helping other people build better lives. Her education in wellness did not happen only in a clinic. It happened through years of IVF, and then through raising a neurodivergent son.

In this conversation we talk about the difference between doing fine and being well. Radhika grew up physically healthy and active. The self-care part came later. A lot of us treat self-care like a fire extinguisher. We grab it after everything is already burning. She wants fireproofing instead: the boundaries you set before you are resentful, the rest you take before you are depleted.

Motherhood was not the plan she practiced for. Unexplained infertility. IVF. Hope and grief on a loop. A son through IVF. A daughter eighteen months later. Then a diagnosis that was not a surprise, and still not the plan. Functioning and being happy are not the same thing. You cannot pour from an empty vessel.

What she built from that is Analyze and Act, and an eight-week program called Bridge to College Independence. Parent track and teen track. Remote. She helps families hand over the real stuff on purpose: appointments, school, identity, when and how to disclose. The work is as much about parent burnout as teen skills. Autonomy, practiced early, becomes who you are.

We also get into Spoon Theory, the word "yet," task analysis, and why a palm tree outlasts an oak in a storm. I told her the truth about my own social awkwardness, the anxiety loop, and what changed after I learned to forgive myself.

No book. Website: analyzeandact.com. Free college readiness checklist. One-on-ones, and the eight-week course. Always consult your own provider before you change something real.

This is a value-for-value podcast. Support the show at eagertobehealthy.com/support.

Takeaways

- Doing fine is not the same as being well

- Self-care as fireproofing, not a fire extinguisher

- Functioning and happiness can live in two different rooms

- Hand independence to a teen on purpose, before college

- "Yet" turns a wall into a ladder

- Track what fills you and what drains you. No shame. Just data.

Chapters

00:00 Welcome

02:14 Have you always been healthy?

05:18 Have you always been happy?

06:36 IVF, motherhood, and a plan that would not hold

11:36 How her son's diagnosis actually shows up

19:26 Analyze and Act / Bridge to College Independence

26:00 Autonomy, self-forgiveness, and the doomsday spiral

28:45 Spoon Theory and the social battery

32:33 ACT, "yet," and breaking a mountain into steps

39:34 Biggest life skill: oak trees and palm trees

42:04 Where to find her

43:05 Closing

item.title: Eager To Be Healthy - Lorraine Sanborn - Staying Young with a Dog Named Cali
item.description:
Lorraine Sanborn, a healthy aging educator, shares her journey of health transformation and resilience at the age of 72. She discusses the importance of positive social networks, self-care, and the role of companionship in maintaining a healthy and active lifestyle. Lorraine also reflects on her experiences as a caregiver and the valuable life lessons she has learned, promoting aspirational health for individuals over fifty.

Takeaways

  • Resilience and positive mindset contribute to healthy aging.
  • Companionship and pet care play a significant role in promoting an active and fulfilling lifestyle.

item.title: Eager to be healthy - Vanessa Cook - Your Body Isn't Working Against You
item.description:
Vanessa Cook was hospitalized for severe asthma at eighteen months old. By her late twenties she was living with asthma, eleven years of fibromyalgia, and a heart condition nobody had found yet — and she'd been told to expect a pacemaker by forty-five. She's thirty-seven now. No pacemaker, no heart medication, no asthma medication, and a résumé that includes ultramarathons.

In this conversation with Michael Scott Eger, Vanessa traces the turning point: the night her husband told her, through tears, that he was afraid he'd end up raising their children alone. What followed wasn't one fix. It was a five-mile obstacle course she had no business entering, two and a half hours of vomiting and crying, and a finish line that taught her she could do hard things — as long as she stopped trying to do them all at once.

We get into why the trendy protocols failed her, how she learned that even a "healthy" food can be the wrong food for a specific body, and why she now reads symptoms as messages rather than problems to silence. Vanessa also makes the case for whole-person care — the emotional and spiritual work a fifteen-minute appointment will never reach — and for walking into that appointment educated enough to ask, "can we try this first?"

Vanessa Cook is the founder of Starlight & Sage Wellness. Learn more at starlightandsagewellness.com.

Eager to Be Healthy is listener-supported and ad-free. Support the mission at eagertobehealthy.com/support.

Takeaways

  • A symptom is a signal. Medicating it away can cost you the information underneath it.
  • No protocol is universal. Vanessa's turnaround started when she stopped chasing trends and started paying attention to her own body.
  • Your doctor gets fifteen minutes with you a year. You get 24/7. Showing up educated changes the conversation.
  • Capability is built in small decisions, not dramatic ones. The finish line mattered less than the eight years after it.

Chapters

00:00  Overcoming Health Challenges
02:16  What Started the Journey
03:15  The Hidden Heart Condition
16:16  The Bluff Mudder
23:15  The Whole Body Approach
26:54  Advocating for Yourself
29:08  Working with Vanessa Cook

item.title: Eager to be Healthy - Matt Robinson - Afib - Writing - Boxing - Teaching in Jails
item.description:
Matt Robinson, a writer and boxing teacher, shares his journey in health, wellness, and teaching in the prison system. He discusses his genetic health challenges, mental health techniques, and the impact of his work on his well-being. Matt also talks about his writing projects, ADHD, and his passion for boxing.

Takeaways

  • Genetic health challenges
  • Mental health techniques
  • Impact of work on well-being

item.title: Eager To Be Healthy - Allie Chandler From Lyme to Wellness
item.description:
Eager to Be Healthy — Allie Chandler — From Lyme to Wellness

At twenty-five, Allie Chandler left for a backpacking trip through Europe as a healthy young teacher, and she came home with thirty to forty rotating symptoms that arrived all at once and refused to be named. It would take four more years to learn that a cluster of bug bites at the base of the Swiss Alps had sent her home with Lyme disease and several co-infections.

In this conversation, Allie walks Michael through what those years asked of her — the specialists who ruled things out one by one, the heart rate that leapt from 55 to 160 the moment she stood up, and the energy healer who finally asked the question no physician had thought to ask. She shares what actually moved her toward wellness, too: a physical protocol built on drainage support, six months of daily limbic system retraining, and a slow rebuild of strength that started with putting on a pair of tennis shoes and sitting back down. None of the three worked alone. Together, over time, they gave her body somewhere safe enough to heal.

Allie is now the founder of Upsell Health, where she helps practitioners and wellness brands speak to people who are sick in a way that leaves them feeling seen. She calls it empathy-led marketing, and it comes straight from the years she spent wishing that someone would look at her and say, in her words: "You're not crazy. There's something going on."

Takeaways

  • Healing rarely moves in a straight line — and the good weeks still count
  • Nervous system regulation as the ground that lets a protocol take hold
  • Limbic system retraining, neuroplasticity, and the brain's capacity to rewire
  • Rebuilding strength in the smallest increments a body can accept
  • The real out-of-pocket cost of functional medicine, and the value of talking openly with providers about it
  • Empathy-led marketing: education and honesty in place of urgency

Chapters

  • 00:00 The Onset of Illness
  • 13:37 The Healing Journey
  • 40:12 Transition to Marketing

item.title: Eager to Be He Healthy - Ana Melikian of the Mindset Zone
item.description:
Growing up on a farm in Portugal gave Ana Melikian a head start on healthy living she didn't fully appreciate until years later. In this episode of Eager to Be Healthy, Ana — a psychologist-turned-life-coach and host of The Mindset Zone podcast — joins Michael for a conversation about how culture, real food, and mindset coaching all connect in the pursuit of feeling your best.

Ana shares how her upbringing shaped her relationship with food: cooking from scratch, eating what the family grew, moving naturally every single day. She and Michael dig into why preparing your own meals — even simple ones — helps your body digest better and gives you a natural sense of how much is enough. They even get into why cracking nuts out of the shell is a surprisingly good health strategy.

From there, the conversation shifts to mindset. Ana explains how the thoughts running on autopilot in your head shape your choices in ways you don't even notice — and how focusing on wellness, rather than what's going wrong, literally pulls you toward healthier patterns. This isn't abstract philosophy: it's practical, warm, and immediately usable.

If you've ever felt stuck knowing what to do but struggling to actually do it, Ana's perspective on choice, habit, and personal history will meet you right where you are.

Follow Eager to Be Healthy on Apple Podcasts or Spotify and never miss a conversation that helps you live well from the inside out.

Takeaways

  • Cultural diversity shapes individual experiences
  • Healthy habits are influenced by upbringing and lifestyle
  • The ritual of eating and digestion impacts overall health
  • Transitioning from clinical psychology to life coaching
  • International differences in mental health care
  • The relationship between happiness and health
  • The power of choice and mindset
  • Creating new perspectives and overcoming change
  • The Mindset Zone Podcast and meditation
  • Embracing uniqueness and entrepreneurship

item.title: Eager to be Healthy—Mike Dyson, a health scare and faith, built a gym empire.
item.description:
A Marine, a gym owner, and still not bulletproof. Mike Dyson built an Anytime Fitness franchise after years of walking through back pain. Then a double bypass hit him right when he looked healthy. If you have ever wondered how faith, fitness, and a hard past can share one life, this episode is for you.

Mike Dyson lives in Pensacola, Florida. Former Marine, about twelve years. Anytime Fitness franchise owner. He had five gyms. He sold two and kept three. Author of The Shadow. Four kids. Eleven grandkids.

The story starts with a health challenge in the early 2000s. Major lower back pain. Not a surgery candidate. In 2004, in a church service, he felt called to change his health. He started walking a treadmill every day in pain. Little by little he got better. That path led him into fitness as a business, not only as a hobby.

Before the gyms came the void. His father left before he was born. His mother nearly ended the pregnancy. A lonely childhood with a lot of empty space. Later he filled that void the usual ways people try. After he rededicated his life in 1993, the first thing he heard was to stop blaming. Forgiveness first. Keep your own heart clean. He asked his family to forgive him, reconciled with his stepdad, and eventually reconnected with his biological father before a freak accident took that second chance away.

Then came the scare that does not care how fit you look. In 2023, days before his sixty-third birthday, he had a minimally invasive double bypass. Eight weeks later he was back on the tennis court. Eight months later the emotional weight caught up. Fitness does not make you bulletproof. Faith does not erase the valley. It walks you through it.

His book, The Shadow, comes from Psalm 23 and Psalm 91. Not death as the whole story. The shadow of death. Presence in the dark places. Trauma, ministry, and the long work of healing what rejection started.

Find Mike at mikedysonauthor.com. Book: The Shadow.

This is a value-for-value podcast. Support the show at eagertobehealthy.com/support.
Always consult your healthcare provider before making changes based on health content.

Takeaways
- Looking healthy is not the same as being well
- Rejection early can drive a lifetime of void-filling
- Forgiveness cleans your heart first, not theirs
- Small daily movement in pain can still change the path
- A bypass can hit the body first and the emotions later
- The valley is walked through, not skipped
- Faith and fitness can share the same story without pretending either is magic

item.title: Eager to Be Healthy First Radio Interview
item.description:
The conversation covers a range of topics related to health coaching, nutrition, and food sensitivities. Michael Eager shares his personal health journey, motivation for change, and approach to health coaching. The discussion also delves into the impact of food choices on health, digestive health, and the implications of food processing on nutrition. Additionally, there is a segment on beer brewing and its health implications, as well as a focus on the health coaching model and dietary choices. The conversation covers topics related to healthy eating on a budget, the process of health coaching and client qualification, lifestyle change and weight loss, and the duration and cost of health coaching. Michael Eager, a health coach, shares insights on these topics and provides valuable information on customized health coaching and healthy eating options for individuals on a budget.

Takeaways

  • Health coaching approach
  • Nutrition and food sensitivities Healthy eating on a budget
  • Customized health coaching
